question: Is ETF-flow persistence still one of the framework's strongest documented decision edges when historical decisions are replayed using only ETF information that was actually knowable at each decision timestamp?
hypothesis: The defensive value of ETF outflow persistence survives strict knowledge-time correction, while positive ETF inflows remain substantially weaker as offensive evidence.
baseline: Existing canonical Sensor Audit / ETF asymmetry learning evaluated against true point-in-time ETF vintages rather than latest-vintage hindsight.
required_analysis: Reconstruct decision-time ETF knowledge states using observed_at, verification time, revision chains and knowledge_time_status.
Compare first-known, first-complete, settled-double-read and latest-vintage values where evidence permits.
Measure decision divergence for historically material warning/market-state episodes.
Quantify warning lead time, false positives, false negatives and directionally material sign/value revisions.
Test the asymmetric claim that ETF outflows have higher decision value than ETF inflows.
Separate source-integrity failure from signal-quality failure.
Preserve UNKNOWN where knowledge time cannot be proven.
falsifier: The ETF-warning advantage materially disappears, reverses, or becomes non-reproducible when only point-in-time knowable vintages are allowed.
kill_condition: If corrected ETF evidence adds no reproducible decision divergence beyond existing price/breadth/rotation owners, demote the sensor from claimed decision edge to context/crosscheck.
forbidden: latest-vintage values treated as if known historically
